source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Wisconsin technical college opens $3.5M dental clinic for hygiene and assistant training
summary: Mid-State Technical College has opened a $3.5 million dental clinic in Wisconsin Rapids to support its new dental hygiene and dental assistant programs. The program will take up to 10 students in each field per semester, and the clinic includes simulation labs, dental imaging rooms and dental chairs. Hygiene students are currently in entry-level courses and will start hygiene program classes in the fall.
why: The new training capacity adds to the pipeline of hygienists and dental assistants, and the college credited feedback and engagement from the local dental community, which may create opportunities for practices to partner with the program.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Five dentists take on new leadership roles across DSOs, schools and associations
summary: Smile Brands promoted Jason Genta, DDS, to senior vice president of clinical operations. Thomas Paumier, DDS, was installed as the 163rd president of the American Dental Association, and Nova Southeastern University named Andres Pinto, DDS, DMD, dean of its College of Dental Medicine effective Jan. 2. The roundup also notes that Marcelo Araujo, DDS, PhD, was elected to the FDI World Dental Federation's Science Committee and that the Minnesota Dental Association installed John Noack, DDS, as president for the 2026-27 term.
why: Changes in leadership at DSOs, dental schools and professional associations can shift the clinical direction, education priorities and policy agenda that affect how practicing dentists work and train the next generation.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Videa's dental AI imaging tools will reach Canadian practices via ClearDent
summary: Boston-based Videa has partnered with British Columbia-based ClearDent, a dental practice management platform, to bring Videa's AI imaging into ClearDent's software in Canada. Radiographs captured in ClearDent can be automatically analyzed by Videa's AI, with findings meant to support patient education and treatment acceptance. Videa is the first AI imaging partner to launch through ClearDent's Embedded Experience program.
why: Dentists using ClearDent in Canada may gain access to AI-assisted radiograph analysis inside their existing practice management system, which could affect how findings are explained to patients and how treatment is presented.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Ranking of US dental schools by 2025-26 graduate count released by ADA data
summary: Based on American Dental Association data for the 2025-26 academic year, New York University led the list of dental schools by number of graduates, followed by Tufts University and Boston University. The article lists the top 10 schools, with the ranking ending at Midwestern University with 142 graduates.
why: Dentists and dental specialists considering where to recruit new graduates or where to train may find this graduate-volume data useful for understanding the pipeline of incoming dentists.

headline: Scoping review sorts evidence on 3D-printed versus thermoformed aligners and retainers
summary: A recent scoping review examined studies on thermoformed and 3D-printed orthodontic appliances and their materials. It notes that laboratory, ageing and safety findings are often presented as if they matter as much as patient studies, which can leave clinicians relying on manufacturers' claims. The review aims to clarify what can be concluded about appliance performance and which clinical questions remain open.
why: Dentists who prescribe or fabricate aligners and retainers can use this review to judge how much weight to give lab data versus clinical studies when choosing between appliance types.

headline: Reexamining tissue-level implants for front-tooth aesthetic cases
summary: A new clinical article revisits the use of tissue-level implants in anterior restorations, where their role remains debated. The debate centers on limited control over the emergence profile and the possibility of implant collar exposure. The authors argue for their use by examining possible biological and mechanical benefits of the design.
why: Clinicians placing implants in visible front-tooth sites may find this a useful reference when weighing tissue-level designs against alternatives for aesthetic outcomes.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Specialized Dental Partners reaches 200 partnerships across 37 states
summary: Franklin, Tennessee-based Specialized Dental Partners has marked its 200th partnership. The DSO began in 2018 as US Endo Partners, focused only on endodontists, then expanded into other specialties and was renamed in 2023. According to the company, its network now includes more than 450 doctors and 2,500 team members across 37 states.
why: Growth of specialty-focused DSOs like this one signals increasing consolidation among specialty practices, which may affect how independent specialists weigh partnership options.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Former Aspen Group sales executive named COO of Southern Orthodontic Partners
summary: Nashville-based Southern Orthodontic Partners has appointed Sarah Sharfstein as its chief operating officer. She previously held leadership roles over eight years at The Aspen Group, most recently as vice president of sales enablement and sales effectiveness, and spent more than a decade at Align Technology. The DSO supports more than 120 practices across the southern U.S.
why: The hire of a leader with sales and operations experience from large dental companies signals how DSOs are staffing their management teams to support their growing networks of practices.

headline: Videa's AI imaging joins ClearDent software for Canadian dental practices
summary: Videa and ClearDent announced a partnership that brings Videa's AI-assisted radiographic analysis into ClearDent Imaging. Radiographs captured in ClearDent can be analyzed automatically and securely, with findings shown alongside patient images and treatment information. Videa is the first AI imaging partner to launch through ClearDent's Embedded Experience framework.
why: Dentists using ClearDent in Canada may be able to review AI-assisted imaging findings within their existing software, which could help them explain findings and recommended care to patients more clearly.

headline: China's second dental implant bulk procurement round weighs quality alongside price
summary: Chinese healthcare authorities are putting more weight on product quality in the second round of volume-based procurement for dental implants and related consumables, which launched on 28 September. Sichuan province is leading the implant contract renewals and Shaanxi province is leading those for orthodontic products. Manufacturers that offer a competitive mix of price and quality could receive larger procurement volumes.
why: For dentists and practices sourcing implants in or from China, procurement rules that reward quality as well as price may shape which implant brands are available and at what cost.

headline: Oryx Dental Software Wins 2026 Inc. Power Partner Award
summary: Oryx Dental Software, a cloud-based and AI-powered dental practice management platform, was named a 2026 winner of the Inc. Power Partner Awards. The annual honor recognizes B2B companies that help entrepreneurs and businesses grow through services such as technology, compliance, and marketing. The excerpt notes Oryx was founded by a dentist and combines clinical workflows, patient records, scheduling, billing, and AI tools in one platform.
why: For a practicing dentist, this is a vendor recognition rather than a clinical finding, but it highlights practice management software that aims to reduce workflow complexity so teams can focus on patient care.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Dental M&A deal volume falls 27% from a year earlier in Q3 2026
summary: Levin Associates reported 51 dental transactions in the third quarter of 2026, which it said accounted for 49% of all physician medical group mergers and acquisitions. Dental deal volume fell 7% from the second quarter and 27% from the third quarter of 2025. DSOs made up 30 of the deals, including 16 by private equity-backed DSOs, with Imagen Dental Partners and Heartland Dental among the most active.
why: A slowdown in dental deal activity, especially among DSOs and private equity-backed groups, signals shifting competition and buyer interest that could affect practice sale and partnership options.

headline: Dentsply Sirona Reports Progress Five Years Into Its BEYOND Sustainability Strategy
summary: Dentsply Sirona is marking five years of its BEYOND sustainability strategy, which is built on the pillars Healthy Planet, Healthy Smiles, and Healthy Business. The company says it has made strong progress toward its 2025 goals, has exceeded its target of 25 million smiles, and has cut Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity by more than 30% against the 2019 baseline. It is also setting new ambitions for 2030.
why: For a practice, the manufacturer's push on reduced packaging waste and longer equipment lifespan through service and repair may affect how dental products and equipment are sourced, maintained, and replaced.

headline: National Norwegian study examines quality of life among oral health professionals
summary: A British Dental Journal article reports a national study of professional quality of life among oral health professionals in Norway. The excerpt contains only the title and citation, so its findings are not available here.
why: Dentists and their teams may find this study useful for understanding how working conditions affect professional well-being across the oral health workforce.

headline: Solventum launches redesigned Filtek Matrix system for conservative anterior composites
summary: Solventum has made available a next-generation Filtek Matrix restorative system, built on matrix technology first introduced in 2022. The redesign adds a new delivery system meant to make placement and cleanup more efficient, and it works with a digital workflow and Solventum's restorative materials. Through its Clarity Portal planning platform, clinicians receive patient-specific treatment plans, and a customized 3D-printed matrix is then used to guide placement of Filtek restoratives.
why: Dentists placing anterior composites may find that a more efficient matrix delivery and cleanup process could save chair time and support conservative, natural-looking restorations for patients.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Vitana Pediatric & Orthodontic Partners adds Hollis Orthodontics in Louisiana
summary: Vitana Pediatric & Orthodontic Partners, a Fort Lauderdale-based group, has added Hollis Orthodontics in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to its network, according to an October 19 LinkedIn post. The practice is led by Bryan Hollis, DDS. The group, which supports practices in 10 states, earlier added Saratoga Investment Corp. as a debt financing partner in June to fund its growth.
why: It shows continued consolidation by dental support organizations, which may matter to independent orthodontic and pediatric practices weighing affiliation or financing options.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: WVU School of Dentistry receives $15M federal award for renovations and equipment
summary: The West Virginia University School of Dentistry in Morgantown received a $15 million Congressionally Directed Spending award through the Health Resources and Services Administration. Sen. Shelley Capito, who helped secure the funding, announced it in an October 20 release, and the money will go toward dental school renovations and equipment purchases. The school had also received $12.6 million in 2024 for an expansion and renovation project.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Five dentists weigh in on how vertical integration will reshape dental care
summary: Becker's Dental Review gathered views from five dental leaders on vertical integration, prompted by Optum's recently awarded $30 billion VA dental contract. The article notes that payers and large health systems are moving deeper into dentistry, and that dental executives expect financial performance to determine which practices survive. The excerpt also cites VA figures showing more than 800,000 veterans received dental care through the VA in fiscal year 2025.
why: Dentists should expect growing pressure from large payers and health systems, which could affect practice independence, reimbursement, and referral patterns, so financial planning and strategy matter more.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Unified Patent Court sides with Align Technology in Angelalign infringement case
summary: The Unified Patent Court ruled that Angelalign's aligner systems using its Torque Ridges feature infringe Align Technology's Power Ridge patent, and it rejected Angelalign's challenges to the patent's validity. Angelalign must stop offering the systems in 17 countries, recall and destroy infringing products, and pay damages. The ruling can still be appealed, and a separate Chinese court earlier found Angelalign's MasterForce and ATreat systems infringed Align's patent rights.
why: This ongoing dispute between two clear-aligner makers could affect which aligner products are available in Europe and how competition in the market plays out for practices that offer clear aligners.

headline: Dr. Silverman on why the IEEM approach builds patient trust in cosmetic dentistry
summary: In his weekly reflection, Harvey N. Silverman argues that successful cosmetic practices using the IEEM System (Inform, Educate, Empower & Motivate) help patients feel comfortable asking questions and considering options. He says team members should see their role as informing and educating patients rather than selling, so patients can make better decisions. He concludes that reducing uncertainty tends to reduce patient resistance.
why: The piece suggests that framing cosmetic treatment as education rather than sales may help patients feel less pressured and more willing to explore options, which bears on how a practice presents treatment.

headline: AAE Launches Online Marketplace for Endodontic Products and Services
summary: The American Association of Endodontists has launched AAE Marketplace, an online platform at marketplace.aae.org that lists more than 140 solution providers serving endodontists. Members can browse company profiles, explore products and services, access special offers and educational content, and share recommendations.
why: Endodontists and other practitioners now have a specialty-focused place to compare vendors and products, and companies gain another way to reach members beyond annual meetings, trade shows, and traditional advertising.

headline: Sodium Trimetaphosphate Shows Promise for Enamel Protection in Toothpaste Studies
summary: A 2022 Clinical Oral Investigations study found that a toothpaste with 200 ppm fluoride, 0.2% sodium trimetaphosphate (STMP), 16% xylitol, and 4% erythritol gave greater protection against early enamel erosion and better surface-hardness recovery than all other tested formulas, including one with the standard 1,100 ppm fluoride. A 2021 Journal of Dentistry study with 14 volunteers wearing enamel specimens reported that the same combination produced the lowest enamel mineral loss and changed biofilm composition compared with the 1,100 ppm fluoride formula.
why: These early findings suggest phosphate and polyol additives might help fluoride toothpastes do more at lower fluoride levels, which could be worth watching as dentists discuss preventive options with patients, though the excerpt is from a promotional-leaning source and the studies are limited in scope.

headline: Henry Schein to release Q3 2026 results on November 3
summary: Henry Schein will publish its third-quarter 2026 financial results before the stock market opens on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A live webcast of the earnings call will begin at 8:00 AM Eastern, with a replay posted on the company's website afterward. CEO Fred Lowery, CFO Ronald N. South, and senior financial advisor Emmanuel Caprais are scheduled to speak on the call.

headline: Guide Outlines Financing Options and Common Loan Mistakes for Dentists
summary: A guest column by a business development executive at a dental and medical funding firm walks dentists through practice financing before they take on a loan. It covers what to expect, the key questions to ask, and mistakes that can cost practice owners a significant amount over the life of a loan. The excerpt also explains that lenders often treat dental practices differently from other small businesses, with dedicated programs offering features such as little or no money down and longer repayment terms.
why: Dentists planning to buy, start, or upgrade a practice may get better loan terms by understanding dental-specific lending programs and comparing offers carefully before committing.

headline: Podcast on dental evacuation system maintenance, biofilm, and mercury from amalgam
summary: In an episode of Dentistry Today's TEN @ 10 hosted by Dr. Paul Feuerstein, infection control specialist Lori Serna-Pate discusses maintaining evacuation and suction systems. The conversation covers purging versus end-of-day line cleaning, how biofilm and amalgam mercury can affect these systems, and amalgam separators. It also touches on Solmetex cleaning products and training the whole dental team on these procedures.
why: Evacuation system cleaning is an often-overlooked area, and the episode suggests that clear protocols and team-wide training can improve consistency and compliance in the office.

headline: Dietary patterns linked to dental caries in postmenopausal women
summary: A British Dental Journal article published online examines the association between dietary patterns and dental caries experience among postmenopausal women. The excerpt is limited to the title and publication details, so specific findings are not available.
why: Diet may be a factor in caries risk for postmenopausal patients, so dentists may want to review the full paper for dietary counseling points once it is accessible.

headline: Systemic disease burden in adults 40+ attending a UK dental hospital studied via linked records
summary: A cross-sectional study published in the British Dental Journal examined the burden of systemic disease among patients aged 40 and over who attended a UK dental hospital. The authors used linked electronic health record data. The excerpt provided does not include the study's findings.
why: The study focuses on general health conditions in older dental patients, which may be relevant to how dentists consider medical history when treating this age group, though specific results are not available in the excerpt.

headline: INDICATE study to estimate undiagnosed pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes in dental primary care
summary: A British Dental Journal article published online on 19 October 2026 describes the INDICATE study, which aims to estimate how many patients in primary dental care have undiagnosed pre-diabetes or type 2 diabetes. The excerpt contains only the title and publication details, so no findings or methods are available.
why: It points to dental settings as a possible place for diabetes screening, though the excerpt gives no results yet to act on.
